jobs.title: Sr. Consultant, Supplier Risk Management
jobs.description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What you’ll be doing

You are passionate about Information Security and Risk Advisory services and want to join our growing information security group. As a Senior Consultant, Supplier Risk Management you will be responsible for conducting Third Party due diligence assessments to identify potential risks to help our technology and business stakeholders meet security goals and objectives. Utilizing your relationship building skills, you will partner with line of business, Third Party suppliers, technology teams and help them proactively identify potential risks and present recommendations that are practical and achievable.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. You’ll have the flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you’ll spend 1-3 days per week on-site, while other days will be remote

How you’ll succeed
- Advisory/Assessment Services – Conduct ongoing Third Party due diligence, including the review of independent assurance reports to help determine the potential information security risk to CIBC.  Assess business needs against potential risks and provide your recommendations to enhance our information security landscape.

- Delivery and Execution - You will help us execute detailed Information Security risk assessments for key Third Party suppliers, conduct ongoing monitoring of these suppliers and provide detailed reporting/analytics.  Provide direction and remediation directions to Third Parties and business partners.  Maintain and manage third party risk database to ensure proper risk management and proper awareness.

- Communication - Build and present documentation to executive management aimed at communicating potential risks and providing recommendations. Provide feedback to and participate in the design and implementation of security assessment processes across the organization. Research, design, and implement security monitoring practices and operationalize these processes across the group.

Who you are
- You can demonstrate experience in Information Security , Third Party risk assessments, Vulnerability & Penetration testing, and application security development projects (with exposure to Agile Development processes). It's an asset if you have familiarity with the Financial Services industry and experience with cyber assessments on legal firms.

- You have experience in Cloud Computing technologies, use of the Archer GRC tool, External Threat Intelligence tools (specifically Black Kite), and CISSP, CTPRP, CISM, or related cyber certifications are considered assets. (This role will be supporting the Legal LoB.)

- You're passionate about people. You find meaning in relationships, and surround yourself with a diverse network of partners. You build trust through respect and authenticity.

- You're digitally savvy. You seek out innovative solutions and embrace evolving technologies. You can easily adapt to new tools and trends.

- Your influence makes an impact. You know that relationships and networks are essential to success. You inspire outcomes by making yourself heard.

- You give meaning to data. You enjoy investigating complex problems, and making sense of information. You're confident in your ability to communicate detailed information in an impactful way.

- Values matter to you. You bring your real self to work and you live our values – trust, teamwork and accountability.

Prior to starting in this role, security checks, including a criminal record check must be successfully completed to the satisfaction of CIBC. An annual criminal record check may also be required.

jobs.description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

BUSINESS UNIT DESCRIPTION

The Finance group provides financial services to CIBC’s businesses through effective governance and decision support processes. These services include financial, management and regulatory reporting, maintenance of accounting records and internal controls, financial analysis and planning, tax planning and compliance, treasury, global sourcing and payment processing, regular reviews of business line performance, corporate real estate and liaison with CIBC’s investors. In addition, Finance assists Corporate Development in providing financial advice regarding CIBC’s business opportunities and transactions.

LINE OF BUSINESS DESCRIPTION

Finance Shared Services, Singapore is a one stop shop providing the full suite of Finance services to Singapore office. The team performs Financial regulatory, management and statutory reporting, accounts payables and expense accounting and supports taxation. The team provides value by helping clients and partners to make effective decisions, compliance with regulatory and statutory requirements, processing of vendors invoices and staff expenses, participation and support of global and regional projects/initiatives.

Main Objectives

Act as an active support to the Head of Finance, Singapore , providing accurate information and management of staff to carry out the Finance’s functions re expense processing, financial regulatory reporting, statutory reporting, profit and loss reporting, projects and initiatives for Singapore Branch and the Capital Market Service license entity.

Key Responsibilities include:
- To ensure the timeliness and accuracy of both internal and external financial reporting, financial regulatory reporting, statutory reporting, profit and loss reporting and variance analysis.

- To review new products and advise on regulatory and accounting structures and systems.

- Timely preparation and submission of the regulatory reporting requirements to MAS.

- To be responsible for maintaining good working relationships with internal and external auditors, advisors and regulators

- Ensure financial controls (e.g. review of suspense accounts, review of incentive compensation accounts, aged items, reconciliation, application of policy etc.) are applied in a manner that provides accurate financial information.

- Preparation and filing of the Financial statements and assist tax team by providing information as requested for income tax returns as well as the international transfer pricing requirements.

- Maintain financial reporting systems in a manner which aids automation and accuracy and provides timely information to the Head of Finance.

- Participate in projects from Finance perspective to support new products and business lines.

Primary internal and external contacts:
- Head of Finance Australia -  as a line manager

- Head of Finance Singapore – advising on current activities and concerns for finance in Singapore

- Singapore Finance – direct reports, discussing work in progress, new initiatives, review of figures and local staff concerns.

- Tax Group – covering local tax reporting and transfer pricing agreements.

- Internal Audit – in relation to review of financial results and performance of Finance group.

- External Audit – regarding planning reviews and audit work and local accounting issues.

- Regulator – Financial regulatory returns and attending to ad hoc Financial request/queries from Regulators

Qualifications and Experience
- Minimum 5 years of relevant experience in a similar position

- Qualified CPA or equivalent qualification

- MAS regulatory reporting requirements for wholesale banks as well as CMS license to ensure that the requirements are understood and delivered

- Accounting knowledge for Global Markets product like Global Credit Financing, FX, Repo, Bond Trading etc.

- Generally Accepted Accounting Principal covering local requirements to ensure financial records meet the local standards, IFRS/Canadian requirements is preferred

- Diverse product knowledge in general wholesale banking products such as corporate loans, contingents such as bonds/guarantees, deposits, securities, derivatives and foreign exchange, investment banking M&A and underwriting covering business activities in office to ensure proper review and analysis of performance is achieved

- Financial reporting systems including source systems in order to provide efficient use and maintenance of the systems from a financial reporting perspective and ensuring that proper control and reconciliation is undertaken

Reporting to the Director-Governance and Controls, the Manager, Governance and Controls, will play a significant role in the implementation of Finance governance, compliance and control initiatives, programs and processes. The Sr Manager of Data Governance you will lead and manage Personal & Business Banking (PBB) data governance activities and will have responsibility for improving the collection of metadata, data quality and managing the protection of sensitive data and information assets. The position will focus on establishing and ensuring adherence to the CIBC data governance policies and procedures. As a Sr Manager you will have a direct impact on the business by helping to define, develop, and maintain business processes for successful data governance and quality within PBB.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. You’ll have the flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you’ll spend 1-3 days per week on-site, while other days will be remote.

How You'll Succeed
- Strategy & Guidance - Provide leadership and guidance on Data Governance initiatives in PBB. Help Establish and govern a data governance implementation roadmap. Facilitate the roll out of PBB wide data governance framework, with a focus on improvement of data quality and the protection of sensitive data through modifications to organization behavior policies and standards, principles, governance metrics, processes, related tools and data architecture. Define roles and responsibilities related to data governance and ensure clear accountability for stewardship of the company’s principal information assets in accordance with Enterprise Data Governance policies. Interface with senior management and contribute towards ongoing data quality improvement initiatives and ensuring that issues are escalated accordingly and in a timely manner. Contribute to successful completion of data governance project deliverables. Participate in project and team meetings, interact and collaborate with team members and other departments as appropriate. Participate in PBB Data Governance Council meetings providing program updates, informing of Policy and Standard changes, identification of quality issues, review of data intensive projects, status of remediation efforts and other program activities.

- Process Management - Serve as a liaison between Business and Functional areas and technology to ensure that data related business requirements for protecting critical data are clearly defined, communicated and well understood and considered as part of operational prioritization and planning. Maintain artifacts, including but not limited to, an inventory of applications, data governance roles, Data Governance Council materials, Data Sharing Agreements (DSA), Data Sharing Risk Assessments (DSRA), Deviations & Deficiencies tracking, escalations, data dictionaries. Facilitate the development and implementation of data quality standards, data protection standards and adoption requirements across PBB.

- Reporting & Analytics - Define indicators of performance and quality metrics and ensure compliance with data related policies, standards, roles and responsibilities, and adoption requirements. In conjunction with the data stewards, provide progress reports to management and oversee periodic updates to the PBB Data Governance procedures. Lead the remediation of data governance deficiencies across PBB. Monitor adherence to data policies across the organization to ensure availability of high-quality data, consultative and subject matter expertise, ensuring all users of data understand policies, procedures and standards. Provide regular status reports to senior management regarding ongoing data management activities, performance metrics, issues and other program activities to enable awareness and tracking of program compliance and remediation efforts.

Who You Are
- You can demonstrate a minimum of 5 years’ experience in supporting enterprise wide data governance including measuring/monitoring data quality, recommending improvements in data, data governance capabilities such as metadata ingestion, data mapping, business lineage & traceability, policy management, governance/quality metrics development & reporting, workflow and issue management, data stewardship management (roles and responsibilities), data classification and/or data catalogue management. The Energy, Infrastructure, & Transition (“EIT”) team provides investment banking services to existing and prospective clients in the power, utilities, renewables, infrastructure, midstream, upstream energy, and energy transition sectors. Our client-centric approach incorporates M&A and other financial advisory services with full access to the debt, equity and loan capital markets. The team also delivers complex risk and hedging solutions to clients. The EIT team manages a market leading platform from our offices in New York, Houston, Toronto, Calgary, London, and Bogota. Our New York office is the largest in EIT’s global footprint.

EIT’s coverage universe across the power, utilities, infrastructure, and energy sectors provides the opportunity to play an integral role advising on significant and marquee transactions that support the AI build-out and broader re-industrialization of North America. The team’s coverage mandate includes conventional and renewable power, regulated utilities and utility infrastructure, infrastructure, midstream, upstream energy, and energy transition. The EIT team supports our clients through a variety of transactions including M&A, strategic advisory, capital structure advisory, equity and debt capital financings, and tax equity transactions.

The EIT team is a leading advisor in the power, utilities, and renewables sectors maintaining a top 5 position in the North American M&A league tables.

With guidance from Managing Directors, Executive Directors or Directors, the Analyst will complete assignments that help our clients achieve their goals and impact the CIBC's bottom line through transaction and financing execution, client relationship support, industry and company research, and contributing to the overall communication flow across our global offices. jobs.description:

BUSINESS UNIT DESCRIPTION

CIBC Capital Markets delivers Sales & Trading, Investment Banking and Corporate Banking solutions, and top-ranked research, to institutional, corporate and government clients across Canada, the United States, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
Supervision & Governance (S&G) is cross-functional 1st Line of Defence unit specialising in Market Conduct. S&G proactively supports the Capital Markets businesses through a range of independent oversight activities including Controls & Assurance, Trade Surveillance, Communication Surveillance and Conduct Supervision.

JOB PURPOSE

As Capital Markets continues to experience strong growth across its Asia-Pacific franchise, an exciting opportunity has emerged to play a leading role in the enhancement and execution of a smart, sustainable and effective Supervision Framework.

The Regional Lead will serve as an individual contributor and will be responsible for driving the execution of the Regional Supervision Programme and ensuring the region’s Market Conduct and Client Protection risks are effectively identified and controlled. This a broad role that will require a combination of hands-on execution of supervisory controls, investigation of alerts or breaches escalated by other control partners, driving local thematic reviews and risk assessments, and overseeing local Business Supervisors to ensure they discharge their oversight duties effectively.

The successful candidate will be the primary owner and point of contact for all regional 1st line Risk & Control matters.

The role requires a self-starter used to operating independently, comfortable in working closely with Senior Management and Business Heads and driving practical risk and control outcomes in a fast-paced, front-office environment.

The regional focus of the role is on the Asia-Pacific Region, although the Regional Lead will also support some Global and European initiatives.

Key Responsibilities

Risk & Control
- Execute a suite of independent supervisory controls to identify Market Conduct and Client Protection risks.
- Analyse trading, supervisory and surveillance data to identify unusual patterns, emerging risks, policy breaches and control weaknesses.
- Investigate control exceptions and conduct-related incidents, determining root causes and appropriate remediation actions.
- Partner with Trade Surveillance and Communications Surveillance teams to investigate alerts, exceptions and potential breaches.
- Collaborate closely with Sales and Trading Desks to continuously assess and enhance the 1st line control environment.

Supervision
- Oversee the Asia-Pacific Capital Markets Supervision Framework, ensuring Regional Management and Desk Heads maintain effective supervision of employees in accordance with local regulatory requirements and CIBC policies and standards.
- Maintain real-time oversight of employee conduct across Capital Markets and ensure Business Supervisors carry out appropriate investigation and remediation of any conduct concerns, policy violations and control deficiencies.
- Provide independent oversight of management actions taken in response to employee misconduct, control breaches, surveillance alerts, complaints and other supervisory events.
- Complete the quarterly conduct-reviews with Business Supervisors, ensuring all relevant compliance, risk and conduct matters owned by the Desk are accurately recorded and closed-out.
- Monitor the effectiveness of desk-level supervisory practices and challenge Business Supervisors where oversight obligations or best practices are not being discharged appropriately.
- Support Business Heads in understanding emerging conduct, client protection and regulatory risks affecting their businesses, while reinforcing ownership and accountability within the first line.

Governance
- Maintain and enhance S&G’s regional supervisory policies, procedure and governance frameworks.
- Support S&G’s Governance of Algorithmic Trading in the region, including the assessment of new applications and oversight of existing algorithmic trading systems.
- Develop and deliver supervisory reporting, control dashboards and management information for senior management and governance committees.
- Support internal audits, compliance reviews, regulatory examinations and inquiries relating to supervisory controls, market conduct and client protection risks.
- Represent the Supervision & Business Risk function at governance forums and working groups across the region.
- Drive enhancements to supervisory controls, reporting and monitoring capabilities through data analytics, automation and process improvement.

Horizon Scanning
- Identify emerging Market Conduct and Client Protection risks arising from changes in business strategy, client activity and regulatory expectations.
- Monitor and review publications, directives and enforcement actions issued by Asia-Pacific regulators and assess impact on the regional control environment.
- Conduct thematic reviews and targeted assessments of higher-risk businesses, products, trading strategies and supervisory processes.
- Leverage findings from investigations, complaints, surveillance activity and control reviews to identify recurring themes and opportunities for control enhancement.
- Contribute to the ongoing development and strategic evolution of the Asia-Pacific Supervision Programme.

Qualifications & Experience

Required
- Significant experience within Capital Markets, gained in Supervision, Business Risk & Control, Trade Surveillance, Compliance Advisory or related field.
- Strong understanding of the characteristics and trade cycle of one or more FICC products and/or Equity Derivatives.
- Strong understanding of Market Abuse, Client Protection and Internal Fraud risks within Wholesale Banking and Institutional Sales & Trading.
- Experience conducting investigations involving trading activity, employee conduct violations, surveillance alerts or policy breaches.
- Experience designing, implementing or overseeing control frameworks within a regulated financial institution.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret large datasets and identify meaningful trends and risk indicators.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to engage credibly with senior stakeholders.
- Ability to operate independently with limited day-to-day supervision and exercise sound judgement in complex situations.

Preferred
- Experience working directly with front-office Sales and Trading businesses.
- Experience in Trade Surveillance, Communications Surveillance, Front Office Supervision or Market Conduct Risk.
- Knowledge of regulatory requirements for Wholesale Banking and Sales and Trading in Hong Kong and/or Singapore.
- Experience supporting regulatory examinations, internal audits and remediation programmes.
- Familiarity with data visualisation and analytics tools.
- The ability to read Traditional Chinese or Japanese regulatory publications would be an advantage, but not essential.

What We're Looking For

The successful candidate will combine strong technical expertise with a pragmatic and collaborative approach. They will be comfortable analysing trading data, investigating conduct concerns and executing supervisory controls, while also building trusted relationships with Business Heads and senior stakeholders across the region.

Success in the role requires:·
- A strong sense of ownership and accountability.
- The ability to work autonomously and drive outcomes independently.
- Strong investigative instincts and intellectual curiosity.
- A practical, solutions-oriented approach to risk management.
- The confidence to challenge constructively when required.
- The ability to build credibility with front-office leaders and influence outcomes through partnership rather than authority alone.
- A commitment to fostering a culture of strong supervision, ethical conduct and fair client outcomes.

This is a highly visible role with significant exposure to regional and global business leadership and offers the opportunity to play a leading role in shaping the future of Capital Markets supervision across Asia-Pacific.

Support and manage credit relationships for a portfolio focused initially towards large European fund managers and a number of European banks.  In time, it would be expected that the candidate will adopt responsibility for other NBFI industries as well as banks in other jurisdictions.

Work with trading floor businesses to structure credit facilities to mitigate credit risks inherent in derivatives and other trading floor business products.

Main Objectives
·       Responsible for conducting in-depth counterparty, industry and portfolio analysis supporting the credit relationships for a portfolio initially focused towards large European fund managers and a number of European banks.

·       Build and maintain relationships with CIBC marketers/traders, and respond quickly to requests for credit facilities from the trading floor.
·       Provide expertise in the area of credit risk associated with trading floor business products.

arrangements and appropriately identifying any relevant changes in the financial
condition/business of a client.

·       Ensure that the portfolio meets with appropriate risk management guidelines and remains current with the changing methodologies.

·       Must have a good knowledge of derivative products and seek to develop a more in depth knowledge of them and other bank products, and partner with trading floor personnel to deliver timely results for clients.

·       Must be able to assess factors which affect the risk profile of a customer quickly in order to make timely decisions and take appropriate action as necessary.
·       Good analytical skills including experience in analysing financial statements in order to assess credit risks.

·       Focused attention to detail when reviewing financial information and preparing credit applications.
·       Work in a team environment where sharing of skills and knowledge is critical.
·       Good oral and written communication skills to effectively communicate to stakeholders and senior management.

Sound knowledge of derivatives documentation, notably ISDA/CSA
